The Story of Queen Chelini and King Shrenik

I bow to Lord Jina, who is the god of gods of the entire world and whom the gods of heaven worship with devotion, and I write the story of the power of right faith through Maharanee Chelini and Shrenik.

Upshrenik was king of Magadh. Rajgriha was then the special capital of Magadh. Upshrenik's queen was Suprabha. Shrenik was her son. Shrenik was as handsome as he was endowed with many virtues. He was intelligent, very grave in nature, brave, generous, and extremely radiant.

Bordering the kingdom of Magadh was the kingdom of a king named Nagdharma. There was an ancient enmity between Nagdatt and Upshrenik. Nagdatt always looked for an opportunity to take revenge, but at this time there was no serious conflict. He remained a friend of Upshrenik through deceit. This was why he once sent Upshrenik a wicked horse as a gift. The horse was so unruly that it would not move normally, but with just a slight touch of the heel or pull of the reins, it would fly like the wind. There is no wonder that the wicked are like this.

One day, Upshrenik mounted this very horse and went out for a ride. As soon as he pulled the reins, the horse flew like the wind. After a long time, it stopped in a forest. The owner of that forest was a Bhil named Yamdand, who was truly as fearsome as Yama, the god of death. He had a daughter named Tilakavati. Tilakavati was very beautiful. It would not be wrong to say that a diamond had been found in a coal mine. Where was the black, terrifying Yamdand, and where was his daughter Chandravati Tilakavati, who could shame the celestial nymphs of heaven!

Seeing this world-beautiful form, Upshrenik was captivated. He proposed to Yamdand for Tilakavati's hand. Yamdand replied, 'O emperor, there is no doubt that I am very fortunate, when an emperor of the earth becomes my son-in-law. And I am extremely happy. Before I give my daughter in marriage to you, you must accept one condition — that you give the kingdom to the child born of Tilakavati.' Upshrenik accepted Yamdand's condition. Yamdatt then, according to his promise, gave his daughter in marriage to him.

Upshrenik returned to Rajgriha with Tilakavati. In time, a son was born to them, who was named Shrenik. Shrenik grew up to be wise, brave, and virtuous. Through the power of his mother's right faith and his own merit, he became one of the greatest kings and devotees of Lord Jina. He built Jain temples throughout his kingdom, gave generously to monks and the worthy, and ultimately took initiation as a monk, attaining liberation.

This story teaches that right faith, even when it arises from unexpected circumstances, can lead to the highest spiritual goals. Queen Chelini's faith and her son Shrenik's devotion to Jain dharma show that spiritual merit transcends birth and circumstance. The wise should cultivate right faith regardless of their origins, for faith is the foundation of all spiritual progress.
